# ethereum-optimism/op-geth Monthly Report (May 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In May 2026, development on `op-geth` centered on hardening the infrastructure for the Interop Proofs Devnet and resolving persistent flakiness in the CI testing suite. Significant progress was made in refining the "Definition of Done" for interoperability, including the integration of flashblocks and superdispute game play. While the team focused on internal code quality through Engine API refactors, they also addressed critical race conditions in withdrawal proofs and investigated network configuration regressions affecting `op-node` users.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Engine API & Internal Refactoring
Efforts were directed toward improving the maintainability of the codebase by streamlining how the execution layer communicates errors.
*   **Engine API Error Refactor:** A significant refactor was completed within the `eth/catalyst` directory to standardize engine API errors, enhancing code quality and robustness ([#790](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/790)).
*   **Interop Access Lists:** The team transitioned from `supervisor_checkAccessList` to a more specialized `interop_checkAccessList` implementation to better support cross-chain transaction validation ([#791](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/791)).

### Interoperability & Proofs Infrastructure
The project continues to advance the Superchain vision through the Interop Proofs Devnet initiative.
*   **Devnet Milestones:** The "Definition of Done" for the Interop Proofs Devnet ([#20489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20489)) was expanded to include successful superdispute games, conductor re-orgs, and proofs team approval. This network is now designated for long-term internal testing.
*   **Message Validation:** Discussions progressed on implementing unsafe head executing message validation ([#20553](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20553)), with new implementation ideas focusing on 'cross-unsafe' queries and optional failsafes with reorg support.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Kona Activation Fix:** A bug was resolved where the Kona init-chain interop activation gate was incorrectly disabled when `interop_time` was null ([#20578](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20578)).
*   **CI Optimization:** An investigation into using `eatmydata` to speed up CI builds was concluded; the tool was deemed ineffective for the project's statically linked Go binaries ([#20787](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20787)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Flaky Test Suite:** A major focus remains on stabilizing the test suite. `TestWithdrawal_Cannon` ([#19963](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/19963)) and `TestWithdrawal_CannonKona` ([#19964](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/19964)) are undergoing fixes to address race conditions in `GetProof` calls and L1 head timestamp mismatches. Additionally, `TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset` ([#20334](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20334)) continues to show timing issues during execution layer synchronization.
*   **Network Configuration Regressions:** Users reported that "base-mainnet" was missing from `op-node` v1.18.0, forcing some to downgrade to v1.17.0 ([#20810](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20810)).
*   **Mainnet Proofs:** The integration of `op-challenger-runner` with `op-reth` for OP Mainnet is currently blocked pending nodes with enabled proofs history ([#19517](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/19517)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month saw active technical troubleshooting between maintainers and the community, particularly regarding the `op-node` network configuration issue. Collaboration between the `op-geth` and `optimism` monorepo teams remains high, as evidenced by cross-repository PRs for withdrawal fixes ([#20677](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20677)) and the ongoing dependency on the main repository for the deletion of the legacy `op-supervisor` ([#20124](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20124)). Contributors like Inphi have been instrumental in diagnosing complex failure modes in the Cannon-based testing infrastructure.
